title: Virtual Surgical Rehearsal

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Virtual surgical rehearsal uses patient-specific imaging and computational models to let a surgical team practice a planned procedure before entering the operating room. It sits within surgical robotics and navigation, where rehearsal outputs can be transferred to intraoperative guidance. The scope includes preoperative planning, team training, and testing of instrument trajectories or implant placement. It is distinct from generic simulation because it is built from an individual patient's anatomy and pathology.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: It runs on workstations or hospital servers with GPU acceleration for rendering and physics, often linked to picture archiving and communication systems for CT or MRI data. Some setups use haptic devices or robotic consoles to reproduce instrument feel. Cloud-based rehearsal is possible but often limited by data transfer and privacy requirements. The models require segmentation software and sometimes finite element solvers for tissue deformation.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Work begins with segmentation of the patient's scan into bone, vessels, tumor, and soft tissue, then a deformable 3D model is built. The surgeon rehearses steps such as resection margins, screw placement, or anastomosis, with the system recording instrument paths and collisions. Some platforms compare rehearsal metrics to intraoperative navigation, allowing the planned path to be overlaid on live imaging. The method is iterative, as rehearsal findings can lead to revised plans before the real case.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Patient-specific rehearsal models are derived from protected health information, so access, storage, and sharing fall under medical privacy rules. If a rehearsal system is used to guide a procedure, questions of liability can arise when the model is inaccurate or the plan is followed without clinical judgment. Validation and documentation of model fidelity are part of quality management in hospitals. The site tracks active product liability and wrongful death lawsuits against AI companies, which is relevant when rehearsal software is marketed as decision support.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction is toward tighter coupling between rehearsal, intraoperative navigation, and robotic execution, so that a rehearsed plan can be constrained or suggested during live surgery. Improvements in real-time tissue modeling and automated segmentation may reduce preparation time. There is also interest in using rehearsal data to assess surgeon proficiency and to build libraries of case-specific plans, though evidence of patient outcome benefit is still developing.
